name: One-bar transition FX built on a single mod-envelope 'timeline': a rising curve with an end drop drives noise level, full left-to-right pan and a resonant driven filter; an octave-down detuned unison saw on its own amp; a second up-and-down triangle envelope on oscillator sync (~50%); multiband mid distortion; master delay then a sidechain-ducked reverb that blooms after the riser cuts
goal: Design reusable section-transition risers in any synth with drawable envelopes. Choose the length first (usually one bar; half or two bars as needed) and draw a mod envelope from bottom at 0 to top at the bar end, then a steep drop to zero as a safeguard. Use it to raise noise from silence (depth sets loudness), pan from fully left to fully right (set pan hard left, modulate 100%), and open a bright filter with resonance and drive. Add a second voice: a saw an octave down with unison and detune on its own amp and FX bus so each target is controlled separately ('atomized'). Draw a second envelope as a triangle (up then down within the same bar) for oscillator sync (~50% depth). Modulate a multiband distortion's mid band with the timeline. Put tails on the master after distortion: delay with lows and highs cut, then reverb with decay below ~70% and sidechain ducking so the reverb opens up as the riser ends. Optional: stutter/glitch FX before the reverb, a master filter sweep, curve variants and bar-length macros. Distinct from our pitch-ramp and Shepard risers: a multi-target envelope timeline with a ducked tail.

source.title: How to Create Epic Sound FX and Risers That Transform Your Tracks | 100 Sound Design Tips Ep. 13

prerequisites: Synth with drawable multi-point mod envelopes, multiple amps/FX buses, noise and saw oscillators with unison and sync, multiband distortion, delay, reverb with sidechain (Avenger in the source), or Web Audio AudioParam setValueCurveAtTime timelines (implementation note)

inputs.name: curve_shape
inputs.description: Linear, exponential-in, slow-drop or spiky variants

inputs.name: targets
inputs.description: Noise level, pan, filter cutoff, sync, distortion, master filter

outputs.name: transition_fx
outputs.description: Riser/transition that bridges two song sections

outputs.name: patch
outputs.description: Reusable transition patch with swappable envelope curves

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Spoken values: one bar in most cases, pan modulated 100% from hard left, sync ~50%, reverb decay below ~70%. Other depths are by ear.
Modulate per-target levels (separate amps) rather than a master amp, otherwise everything on that amp moves together.
Put delay/reverb after distortion on the master so tails are not distorted; a send would place the reverb before the multiband distortion.
Add a little release to avoid clicks at the end drop.

steps.action: Pick the length (usually one bar). Draw mod envelope 1: start at the bottom at 0, rise to the top at the bar end (4 beats), then add a steep drop back to 0.
steps.expect: A rising control curve with a guaranteed end

steps.action: Noise: oscillator gain at 0, noise level 0, mod envelope 1 → noise level with depth for loudness. Bend the curve for more impact; add a compressor or amp gain if it is too quiet.
steps.expect: Noise swells across the bar and cuts

steps.action: Pan: set noise pan hard left and modulate it 100% with the same envelope (unipolar), so it travels left to right.
steps.expect: Noise sweeps across the stereo field

steps.action: Filter: bright filter with some resonance and drive, cutoff modulated by the same envelope; add a little release.
Second voice: a saw an octave down with unison and detune on a separate amp and FX bus. Its amp level starts at 0 and is modulated by envelope 1.
steps.expect: Detuned body rising under the noise

steps.action: Draw mod envelope 2 as a triangle over the same bar (up to the top then back down) and route it to oscillator sync (~50%). Try curve variants (fast-in or slow-drop before the downbeat).
steps.expect: Sync sweep that peaks and returns within the bar

steps.action: On the second voice's FX bus, modulate a multiband distortion's mid drive with envelope 1.

Master tails after distortion: delay (lows and highs cut, more mix), then reverb with decay below ~70% and sidechain ducking so it stays down while the riser plays and blooms after it cuts. Optional: stutter FX between delay and reverb, a master filter sweep on envelope 1, bar-length macros (4/2/½ bars). Place a low impact/kick on the downbeat.
steps.expect: Transition carries into the next section with a washing reverb tail

verification: The riser level is zero at bar start and ends exactly at the drop point.
A stereo meter shows the noise moving from left to right over the bar.
The sync sweep peaks mid-bar and returns by the end (triangle envelope).
The reverb tail is louder after the riser stops than during it (ducking works).
